promises.label: 2026 NII growth
promises.commitment: Grow full-year NII 5%–7% in 2026 compared with 2025.
promises.outcomeSummary: Management raised 2026 NII growth guidance to approximately 8%, after initially targeting 5% to 7%; full-year results remained pending.

promises.label: Medium-term ROTCE target
promises.commitment: Reach 16% ROTCE around eight quarters from Q1 2026 and the upper end of 16%–18% during the third year.
promises.deadline: Through the third year following Q1 2026
promises.outcomeSummary: Reached 16% and 17% early; latest reported ROTCE was 12.6% (14.9% adjusted). The upper-end medium-term target remained pending.

missing.what_was_said: The CFO reiterated that the ROTCE guidance was a medium-term range, cautioned that every quarter would be different, and said management still needed to keep making progress toward its goal. He also said there were no one-time items to consider in the 16% result.

promises.label: Reduce headcount during 2026
promises.commitment: Reduce headcount during 2026 through attrition and selective hiring.
promises.outcomeSummary: Management reported 3,000 fewer employees than at the start of the year, following reductions through attrition and careful hiring.

resolved.reason: Bank of America’s October 14, 2026 Q3 earnings call reported headcount 3,000 below the year’s start, fulfilling its promise to reduce staffing during 2026.

promises.label: Medium-term operating leverage
promises.commitment: Deliver 200–300 basis points of operating leverage over a 3–5-year period.
promises.outcomeSummary: The medium-term 200 to 300 basis points target remains open despite first-half operating leverage of 450 basis points; management reaffirmed it.

missing.what_was_said: Management raised its 2026 full-year operating-leverage guidance from more than 200 basis points to 300–400 basis points following first-half outperformance. This changed the annual outlook, not the separate 200–300-basis-point medium-term commitment.
Management said "Q3 was slower" and expected to return to operating leverage in Q4, while explicitly keeping the medium-term 200–300-basis-point target unchanged.
